decision: the owner, 2026-10-08, relayed by the build brief: the Beast Ball is the only ball that catches a DUNGEON boss, and only dungeon bosses (Entei today, Heatran and whatever follows); overworld legendaries (the lake trio, the Regis, Lugia and the rest) stay catchable with any ball, so a Master Ball keeps its purpose. x5 on a tagged boss; every other ball refused, the Master Ball included, and handed back; a Beast Ball that fails its roll is consumed as normal. The refusal names nothing. $5,000 a ball at the Cinderlee counter; exempt from blackout loss as the Master Ball is; the jar's crafting recipe closed by our datapack.
research: docs/research/notes/beast-ball-key-1.8.0.md (VERIFIED from the Cobblemon 1.8.0 jar; nothing in it run in game)
rung: datapack (CLAUDE.md principle 6). Cobblemon native supplies the hooks: MoLang callbacks in data/cobblemon/callbacks/<event>/ (pokemon_catch_rate_calculated can set the rate, poke_ball_capture_calculated can refuse after every ball's maths, the Master Ball's included: research note section 3). The species `uncatchable` property refuses every ball or none, so it cannot single out one ball; the species catch rate applies to every ball; the `ultra_beast` label would apply to every Entei in the world. No addon or config key changes a ball's behaviour (no poke_balls data folder, no per-ball config key: research note section 1). Fabric API's resource conditions close the recipe; no custom code anywhere.
tag_why: the world-shaped predicate (CLAUDE.md 'Our list is not the world'): the callbacks key on an entity tag a dungeon boss's own tool puts on it at spawn, never on a species, so an untagged Entei (a raid, a shrine) behaves normally and a new boss joins by tagging itself. Every tool in `bosses` must add it in the same function that binds its boss.
multiplier_why: Cobblemon's own Ultra Beast figure for the Beast Ball (PokeBalls LabelModifier(5.0, true, 'ultra_beast'), research note section 1), so the story and the number agree; about 4 throws on a sleeping boss at 1 HP and 19 at full HP (research note section 5). Applied by set_catch_rate(catch_rate * multiplier), which feeds the jar's own formula, so the status, HP, in-battle and level-gap factors still apply.

refund.why: a refused ball breaks free, and breakFree() discards it with no item (research note section 4): without a refund a refused Master Ball is $27,000 gone. One of the same item is given back, exactly one per refused throw (poke_ball_capture_calculated fires once per capture attempt). Not in creative: PokeBallItem.use takes the ball with ItemStack.consume (method_57008), which does not shrink the stack for a player with infinite materials, so a refund there would make a ball. A Beast Ball is never refunded: its throw was allowed and its failed roll is the price.

recipe_off.mechanism: each id is written back at its own path in our world-local pack (a world datapack sits above the mod's built-in pack, the tools/mega_recipes.py override) holding only `fabric:load_conditions`, which never passes. Fabric API 0.116.14's fabric-resource-conditions-api-v1 (read 2026-10-08 from the snapshot jar): ResourceConditions.CONDITIONS_KEY = "fabric:load_conditions", a list of objects dispatched on the key "condition"; DefaultResourceConditionTypes registers fabric:true (no fields) and fabric:not (field "value"); ResourceConditionsImpl.applyResourceConditions rejects the file; RecipeManagerMixin and ServerAdvancementLoaderMixin apply it to recipes and advancements. Fail closed: were the condition ignored, the file has no recipe or advancement fields and would fail to parse and be skipped.

a ball from an addon whose item id is not its ball id: the refund gives the item named by the ball's ball_type; Cobblemon's own balls are their own items
